status: FROZEN. eval_v2 files (unchanged, byte-identical) plus ptc_headlines. Do not modify; a change means eval_v4.

headlines_llm.what: 70 real news headlines (titles only) from 35 outlets' RSS feeds, fetched 2026-11-14
headlines_llm.annotator: ONE LLM annotator. NOT human annotation; no second annotator; no kappa.
headlines_llm.protocol: Labels were decided from the headline text alone, before any ensemble output on these headlines was seen. Headlines were picked by the annotator from a random sample of 140 (4 random per outlet), so the set is not a random sample of all news and several borderline cases were left out.
caveats: The annotator and the ensemble's models are all general-purpose LLMs: errors may be correlated.
Single annotator: label noise is unknown; some calls are borderline.
Replace or supplement with two human annotators when available.

ptc_headlines.what: 332 real news article titles from the Propaganda Techniques Corpus (PTC), SemEval-2020 Task 11 train split (articles from 2017-2019, mainstream and partisan outlets)
ptc_headlines.annotator: HUMAN: professional annotators, span-level, consolidated by the upstream authors.
ptc_headlines.protocol: Every train-article title, no sampling. no_technique = no propaganda span overlaps the title; one mapped technique = that technique; two or more of ours, or out-of-taxonomy only = excluded; duplicate titles kept once.
ptc_headlines.leakage: No PTC text is in data/dev or the prompt anchors (content-word overlap check: 0 hits). PTC was never used for prompt tuning.
caveats: Titles are annotated as part of the whole article; no_technique means annotators marked no span in the title, not a separate neutrality judgement.
Articles are from 2017-2019, so topics differ from today's RSS headlines.
Rare techniques have tiny supports (1-7); per-technique numbers for them are not meaningful.
